content.title: About
content.content: A fresh cucumber salad sliced thin and tossed with an Italian dressing made from olive oil, vinegar, garlic, oregano, and basil. The dish offers a light, crisp texture and the aromatic notes of Mediterranean cuisine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cucumbers are over 95% water, making the salad an excellent way to stay hydrated.
Italian dressing often includes oregano, which has antioxidant properties.
The traditional Italian "Insalata di cetrioli" is served during summer when cucumbers are at peak harvest.
Cucumber salad can accompany meat dishes or be enjoyed on its own as a light meal.
In some Italian regions, a touch of honey is added to the dressing for subtle sweetness.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: High water content helps maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Low Calorie
items.content: The salad is low in calories, making it suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Cucumbers provide B1, B5, and B7 vitamins that support metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Oregano and basil are rich in polyphenols that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Digestive Support
items.content: Fiber in cucumbers promotes healthy bowel function.

items.title: Allergy to oregano or basil
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to the herbs used in the dressing.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If the dressing is salted, monitor intake, especially for those with hypertension.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Cucumbers can carry pesticide residues; wash them thoroughly before use.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled; you can add sliced radish, cherry tomatoes, or olives. It pairs well with grilled meat, fish, or as a light appetizer.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Stir before serving to evenly distribute the dressing.
